Priya Patel: FYI customer (acme-health) hitting intermittent +200ms tail token latency on their dedicated pool eu-west-2-ded-07 since last night. They say it correlates with other tenants' spikes.
Jordan Kim: any error codes from API?
Priya Patel: 429s rarely, mostly timeouts and long streaming latency. Example: "request timed out after 120s" in app logs. No obvious retry floods.
Mike Hernandez: Can you paste a recent nvidia-smi snapshot from the host? asking if MIG slices are being hot-picked.
Priya Patel: Pasted from customer agent (they're allowed to share):
```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,gpu_name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,power.draw --format=csv
0, A100-SXM4-40GB, 97 %, 78 %, 78 C, 310 W
1, A100-SXM4-40GB, 5 %, 12 %, 52 C, 85 W
```
But the cluster uses MIG 4g. They said one MIG slice shows continuous 100% SM utilization while others are idle.
Jordan Kim: interesting — that screams noisy neighbor on the same physical GPU. Are these dedicated pools heterogeneous (some full-GPU, some MIG)?
Priya Patel: Pool config: reserved-mig=4g:1g:1g (customer requested mixed partitions). Autoscaler didn't add nodes during spike.
Oncall-SRE: Check if autoscaler scale-up is blocked by quota or placement constraints. Also check per-customer capacity token bucket.
Support-Escalations: Customer provided profiler traces showing lots of concurrent short-running sessions from tenant X-123 at 03:12-03:20 UTC. Could be causing continuous context switching on a MIG slice.
Mike Hernandez: Two angles: 1) confirm MIG isolation is configured correctly on node (mps? processes?), 2) verify runtime isn't consolidating small jobs onto same slice due to our scheduler bin-packing.
Jordan Kim: Ran quick query in infra metrics: node eu-west-2-node-43 shows frequent SM saturation spikes aligned with tenant X-123. Also see CUDA context churn in metrics (cuda_context_create rate).
Priya Patel: Customer wants workaround ASAP — they asked if we can move their allocation off the noisy node.
Oncall-SRE: I can evict and reschedule their instances to a different node in the pool. Will that require customer downtime? minimal — streaming sessions will reconnect; recommend a canary move during low traffic window.
Support-Escalations: Any quick config change? e.g., throttle concurrent sessions per-client on that pool?
Mike Hernandez: We have per-customer concurrency cap in pool config but it's currently set high for this customer. We can reduce their max-concurrency from 64 -> 16 temporarily as mitigation.
Jordan Kim: Also consider enabling strict MIG scheduling: avoid packing different tenants into slices of same GPU where possible. That's a scheduler policy change (best-effort today).
Priya Patel: Repro steps for infra if you want to observe:
1) tail streaming logs for tenant X-123 during their peak window.
2) ssh to suspect host and run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` to watch SM memory util.
3) run `kubectl top pod` and `kubectl describe pod` for the affected pods to see throttling events.
4) capture `nvml` counters via our gpu-exporter: `curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep nvml`
Jordan Kim: Good. I also recommend collecting `perf` traces (cuprofiler) for a 1 minute window to catch kernel launches.
Oncall-SRE: I'm going to coordinate a targeted evacuation of the customer's pods off node-43 in ~10m and lower their concurrency cap. I'll post updates here.
Priya Patel: Thanks. Customer asked if this could be due to MIG misconfiguration (e.g., slices overlapping). Any checks?
Mike Hernandez: Run `nvidia-smi mig -lgci` to list MIG instances and ensure they map uniquely to device ids. Also check host kernel driver version; some older drivers had MIG isolation bugs.
Support-Escalations: Customer also raised billing concern: they saw higher token costs due to many retries. Notified billing to freeze charges until we confirm root cause.
Oncall-SRE: Evac in progress — moving 3 pods now.
Infra-Bot: deploy-buddy: started pod-drain for eu-west-2-node-43 at 2025-11-02T03:35:21Z
Jordan Kim: After move, observe SM utilization across GPUs. If noisy tenant still lands on same GPU family, we need to pin tenant to different physical GPU via nodeSelector / topology constraints.
Priya Patel: Post-move: customer reports immediate improvement in tail latency (~70% reduction) for five minutes. Will monitor.
Mike Hernandez: Follow-up actions: 1) audit scheduler packing heuristics for MIG slices, 2) add an anti-affinity rule for tenants with heavy short-lived sessions, 3) add alert for sustained per-slice SM utilization > 85% for > 2m.
Support-Escalations: Noted. Customer will keep us posted.
Priya Patel: I'll keep this thread updated with telemetry and billing outcome. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Oncall-SRE: Marking incident as active -> assigned to Mike for deeper investigation.
Mike Hernandez: Will open a ticket to track scheduler change (SCHED-987) and link this thread.
Support-Escalations: Closing loop with customer for now, will re-open if spike returns.
